title: Naval Communications and Telecommunications Operations MUST-KNOW practice exam

questions.question: What is the primary cause of electrical shock in the human body according to the safety terminology?
options: High Voltage
Electrical Resistance
Electric Current
Static Charge
questions.correct_answer: Electric Current

questions.question: Under what exact environmental conditions must personnel working aloft immediately stop all work?
options: Winds exceed 20 km/h or ship rolls 5 degrees or more
Winds exceed 30 knots / 30 nautical miles or ship rolls 10 degrees or more
Winds exceed 40 km/h or ship rolls 15 degrees or more
Winds exceed 15 knots or ship rolls 8 degrees or more
questions.correct_answer: Winds exceed 30 knots / 30 nautical miles or ship rolls 10 degrees or more

questions.question: Who must personally authorize personnel before they are allowed to go aloft?
options: The Safety Officer
The Officer of the Deck (OOD)
The Commanding Officer (CO)
The Communications Officer (COMMO)
questions.correct_answer: The Commanding Officer (CO)

questions.question: How often must the Officer of the Deck (OOD) pass the aloft warning message over the ship's 1MC while personnel are working aloft?
options: Every 5 minutes
Every 15 minutes
Every 30 minutes
Only once when work begins
questions.correct_answer: Every 15 minutes

questions.question: What is the maximum voltage rating that Navy-issued rubber-insulated safety boots are designed to protect against?
options: 250 volts
440 volts
600 volts
1000 volts
questions.correct_answer: 600 volts

questions.question: According to the study guide, continuous exposure to sound levels at or above what threshold requires the mandatory use of hearing protection?
options: 75 decibels
80 decibels
85 decibels
90 decibels
questions.correct_answer: 85 decibels

questions.question: What are the two basic binary values used to represent discrete information states in digital systems?
options: A and B
0 and 1
High and Low
Positive and Negative
questions.correct_answer: 0 and 1

questions.question: What is the correct sequential order of the basic End-to-End (E2E) communications concept?
options: USER DATA -> SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> ADNS / ROUTING -> ENCRYPTION / FORMAT CONVERSION -> RF EQUIPMENT -> ANTENNA -> TRANSIT LINK -> SHORE / DESTINATION
WORKSTATION -> ADNS -> SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> RF EQUIPMENT -> CRYPTO -> ANTENNA -> SHORE
USER DATA -> ENCRYPTION -> ADNS -> TRANSMITTER -> ANTENNA -> TRANSIT LINK
SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> USER DATA -> ADNS -> TRANSIT LINK -> CRYPTO -> SHORE
questions.correct_answer: USER DATA -> SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> ADNS / ROUTING -> ENCRYPTION / FORMAT CONVERSION -> RF EQUIPMENT -> ANTENNA -> TRANSIT LINK -> SHORE / DESTINATION

questions.question: Which legacy afloat networks and functions are consolidated into the common shipboard infrastructure of CANES?
options: NIPRNet, SIPRNet, JWICS, and CENTRIXS
ISNS, CENTRIXS, SCI LAN, and SUBLAN
NCTAMS, NCTS, and JFTOC
ADNS, IWE, and RF Communications
questions.correct_answer: ISNS, CENTRIXS, SCI LAN, and SUBLAN

questions.question: What is the definition of a 'security enclave' in shipboard network architecture?
options: The physical room housing unclassified network servers
A logically or security separated network domain
An encryption key used exclusively for satellite links
A software program that filters external web queries
questions.correct_answer: A logically or security separated network domain

questions.question: Which of the following describes the primary function of the Automated Digital Network System (ADNS)?
options: It generates and amplifies high-frequency electromagnetic radio signals
It provides physical landline fiber-optic cables to connect a ship to the pier
It is the network routing/traffic-direction part that gets IP traffic to the correct external communications path
It acts as a primary sensor to perform multi-functional target tracking simultaneously
questions.correct_answer: It is the network routing/traffic-direction part that gets IP traffic to the correct external communications path

questions.question: What is the correct order of the afloat data path from a user workstation to a satellite for a Secret e-mail?
options: WORKSTATION -> SWITCH -> EXCHANGE SERVER -> SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> ADNS/PT SIDE -> INLINE ENCRYPTOR -> CT SIDE/ADNS -> CRYPTO/RF EQUIPMENT -> ANTENNA -> SATCOM
WORKSTATION -> ADNS -> INLINE ENCRYPTOR -> EXCHANGE SERVER -> SWITCH -> RF EQUIPMENT -> ANTENNA
WORKSTATION -> SWITCH -> SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> CRYPTO -> INLINE ENCRYPTOR -> ADNS -> ANTENNA -> SATCOM
WORKSTATION -> EXCHANGE SERVER -> SWITCH -> ADNS/PT SIDE -> CRYPTO -> CT SIDE -> ANTENNA -> SATCOM
questions.correct_answer: WORKSTATION -> SWITCH -> EXCHANGE SERVER -> SHIPBOARD NETWORK -> ADNS/PT SIDE -> INLINE ENCRYPTOR -> CT SIDE/ADNS -> CRYPTO/RF EQUIPMENT -> ANTENNA -> SATCOM

questions.question: What is the critical difference between Plain Text (PT) and Cipher Text (CT) in the cryptographic process?
options: PT is analog data; CT is digital data
PT is unencrypted data before the encryption process; CT is encrypted output after the cryptographic process
PT represents low-frequency radio waves; CT represents extremely high frequencies
PT is routed through the NOC; CT is managed by the JFTOC
questions.correct_answer: PT is unencrypted data before the encryption process; CT is encrypted output after the cryptographic process

questions.question: What is the main operational difference between an RF circuit and a transit link?
options: An RF circuit is a physical fiber connection; a transit link is a satellite path
An RF circuit is a radio-frequency communications path; a transit link is the overall path used to transport information between locations
An RF circuit is managed by the NOC; a transit link is managed by the CO
An RF circuit is always unencrypted; a transit link is always encrypted
questions.correct_answer: An RF circuit is a radio-frequency communications path; a transit link is the overall path used to transport information between locations

questions.question: From largest to smallest bandwidth capability, which of the following represents the correct order of E2E SATCOM transit links in the notes?
options: CBSP, NMT, EHF MDR
EHF MDR, CBSP, NMT
NMT, CBSP, EHF MDR
NMT, EHF MDR, CBSP
questions.correct_answer: NMT, CBSP, EHF MDR

questions.question: What are the roles of NCTAMS and NCTS in the shore network architecture?
options: NCTAMS is a major regional area master station; NCTS is a smaller regional/local station that provides infrastructure and services
NCTAMS handles IP networks and services; NCTS handles RF/transit operations
NCTAMS is the unclassified network; NCTS is the secret command network
NCTAMS is located in San Diego; NCTS is located exclusively in Virginia and Hawaii
questions.correct_answer: NCTAMS is a major regional area master station; NCTS is a smaller regional/local station that provides infrastructure and services

questions.question: In shore communications, what is the functional difference between JFTOC and the Network Operations Center (NOC)?
options: JFTOC provides satellite broadband capacity; NOC handles line-of-sight voice circuits
JFTOC handles unclassified e-mail services; NOC handles top secret intelligence networks
JFTOC is the RF/transit communications operations side; NOC manages IP networks and services
JFTOC is a physical cable on the pier; NOC is a wireless space relay
questions.correct_answer: JFTOC is the RF/transit communications operations side; NOC manages IP networks and services

questions.question: What is the correct mapping of DoD networks to their respective security classifications?
options: NIPRNet -> Secret; SIPRNet -> Unclassified; JWICS -> TS/SCI
NIPRNet -> Unclassified; SIPRNet -> Secret; JWICS -> Top Secret / SCI
NIPRNet -> Unclassified; SIPRNet -> TS/SCI; JWICS -> Secret
NIPRNet -> TS/SCI; SIPRNet -> Secret; JWICS -> Unclassified
questions.correct_answer: NIPRNet -> Unclassified; SIPRNet -> Secret; JWICS -> Top Secret / SCI

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct physical relationship between radio wave frequency and wavelength?
options: As frequency increases, wavelength increases proportionately
As frequency increases, wavelength decreases
Frequency and wavelength move in the same direction at all times
Frequency increases while wavelength remains conceptually fixed
questions.correct_answer: As frequency increases, wavelength decreases

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer contains most everyday weather and represents the lowest atmospheric layer?
options: Troposphere
Stratosphere
Ionosphere
Exosphere
questions.correct_answer: Troposphere

questions.question: What major atmospheric region is responsible for long-distance RF communications and undergoes significant day-to-night propagation changes?
options: Troposphere
Stratosphere
Ionosphere
Ozone Layer
questions.correct_answer: Ionosphere

questions.question: What occurs in the ionospheric F region during daylight hours compared to nighttime?
options: It completely disappears during the day due to solar heat
It separates into two distinct sublayers (F1 and F2) during the day and merges into one F layer at night
It remains completely stable during the day but splits into F1 and F2 at night
It sinks down to merge with the Troposphere due to daytime solar ionization
questions.correct_answer: It separates into two distinct sublayers (F1 and F2) during the day and merges into one F layer at night

questions.question: What is the difference between attenuation and conductivity in radio propagation?
options: Attenuation is signal loss; conductivity is how well a surface/material supports electromagnetic energy movement
Attenuation is the bending of waves; conductivity is the bouncing of waves off metallic surfaces
Attenuation is the highest frequency usable; conductivity is the lowest frequency usable
Attenuation occurs in the troposphere; conductivity occurs in the ionosphere
questions.correct_answer: Attenuation is signal loss; conductivity is how well a surface/material supports electromagnetic energy movement

questions.question: What does the Frequency of Optimum Transmission (FOT) represent, and how does it relate to LUF and MUF?
options: The lowest frequency that can support successful communications; lower than LUF
The highest frequency usable; greater than MUF
The best/preferred operating frequency, usable for about 90% of the days in a month; situated between LUF and MUF
The exact average frequency calculated by dividing MUF by LUF
questions.correct_answer: The best/preferred operating frequency, usable for about 90% of the days in a month; situated between LUF and MUF

questions.question: What is the correct order of the nine RF frequency bands from lowest to highest frequency?
options: EHF -> SHF -> UHF -> VHF -> HF -> MF -> LF -> VLF -> ELF
ELF -> VLF -> LF -> MF -> HF -> VHF -> UHF -> SHF -> EHF
ELF -> LF -> VLF -> MF -> HF -> VHF -> UHF -> SHF -> EHF
VLF -> ELF -> LF -> HF -> MF -> VHF -> UHF -> EHF -> SHF
questions.correct_answer: ELF -> VLF -> LF -> MF -> HF -> VHF -> UHF -> SHF -> EHF

questions.question: What three properties of a carrier wave can be modified to modulate information onto a signal?
options: Voltage, Current, and Resistance
Wavelength, Speed, and Velocity
Amplitude, Frequency, and Phase
Propagation, Attenuation, and Polarization
questions.correct_answer: Amplitude, Frequency, and Phase

questions.question: Which of the following lists represents common digital modulation schemes where digital information rides on an analog RF carrier?
options: AM, FM, and PM
FSK, PSK, and QAM
RF, IF, and AF
SYNC, ASYNC, and ISOC
questions.correct_answer: FSK, PSK, and QAM

questions.question: Which digital transmission timing type sends data in separate chunks without a continuously shared clock, relying instead on start and stop indicators?
options: Synchronous
Asynchronous
Isochronous
Co-directional
questions.correct_answer: Asynchronous

questions.question: What is the classic synchronous serial interface rule regarding clocking for DTE and DCE?
options: DTE provides the clocking; DCE uses the provided timing
DCE provides the clocking; DTE uses the provided timing
Both DTE and DCE must independently generate matching clocks with cesium references
The satellite link provides direct clocking to both devices simultaneously
questions.correct_answer: DCE provides the clocking; DTE uses the provided timing

questions.question: What does Eb/N0 compare in digital communications quality metrics?
options: Electrical voltage to background static resistance
Energy used for each information bit (Eb) to noise power spectral density (N0)
The bandwidth of an enclave to the total link bandwidth
Transmitter signal power to receiver antenna polarization mismatch
questions.correct_answer: Energy used for each information bit (Eb) to noise power spectral density (N0)

questions.question: What is the difference between strategic and tactical Navy communications?
options: Strategic supports big-picture national security and theater-level strategy; Tactical supports day-to-day operational fleet tasks
Strategic operates only in port; Tactical operates only while underway
Strategic uses unclassified enclaves; Tactical uses top secret intelligence networks
Strategic uses physical cables; Tactical uses satellite transponders
questions.correct_answer: Strategic supports big-picture national security and theater-level strategy; Tactical supports day-to-day operational fleet tasks

questions.question: Under the Navy RF communications functions, what is the defined range threshold for long-range beyond-line-of-sight (BLOS) communications?
options: Over 10 nautical miles
Over 20 nautical miles
Over 30 nautical miles
Over 100 nautical miles
questions.correct_answer: Over 30 nautical miles

questions.question: What are the key characteristics of UHF SATCOM in Navy communications?
options: High capacity, low mobility, highly secure from jamming
Low capacity, high mobility, easily jammed, and vulnerable to nuclear radiation
Moderate capacity, low mobility, completely unaffected by weather
High capacity, moderate mobility, and highly nuclear-survivable
questions.correct_answer: Low capacity, high mobility, easily jammed, and vulnerable to nuclear radiation

questions.question: What are the three EHF data rate categories listed in the study guide?
options: LDR, MDR, and XDR
SYNC, ASYNC, and ISOC
RF, IF, and DC
AM, FM, and PM
questions.correct_answer: LDR, MDR, and XDR

questions.question: What are the core processes of a transmitter and the four steps of a receiver in order?
options: Transmitter: Generate, Amplify, Modulate; Receiver: Reception -> Selection -> Detection -> Reproduction
Transmitter: Modulate, Demodulate, Receive; Receiver: Select -> Detect -> Amplify -> Reproduce
Transmitter: Encrypt, Compress, Route; Receiver: Decrypt -> Decompress -> Sort -> Display
Transmitter: Generate, Upconvert, Transmit; Receiver: Downconvert -> Filter -> Output -> Listen
questions.correct_answer: Transmitter: Generate, Amplify, Modulate; Receiver: Reception -> Selection -> Detection -> Reproduction

questions.question: What are the three core physical antenna characteristics mentioned in the study guide?
options: Reciprocity, Polarization, and Directivity
Wavelength, Frequency, and Amplitude
Voltage, Current, and Resistance
Reflection, Refraction, and Diffraction
questions.correct_answer: Reciprocity, Polarization, and Directivity

questions.question: How is the coupling/tuning function handled in SHF and EHF satellite antenna systems compared to HF and UHF?
options: SHF/EHF use external manual couplers, while HF/UHF use automated digital couplers
SHF/EHF systems do not use separate couplers; the coupling function occurs internally within the antennas
SHF/EHF use liquid-cooled copper coils, while HF/UHF systems require no couplers at all
SHF/EHF coupling is handled on shore at STEP sites via terrestrial wide area networks
questions.correct_answer: SHF/EHF systems do not use separate couplers; the coupling function occurs internally within the antennas

questions.question: What is the designation of the Simple Key Loader (SKL) fill device used to load Cryptographic Keying Material (KEYMAT)?
options: KY-58
KIV-7M
PYQ-10
KG-175D
questions.correct_answer: PYQ-10

questions.question: What are the basic functions of a multiplexer and a demultiplexer?
options: Multiplexer combines multiple separate signals into one composite signal; Demultiplexer separates a composite signal into its component signals
Multiplexer converts digital signals to analog; Demultiplexer converts analog signals to digital
Multiplexer encrypts plain text; Demultiplexer decrypts cipher text
Multiplexer routes IP addresses; Demultiplexer translates domain names
questions.correct_answer: Multiplexer combines multiple separate signals into one composite signal; Demultiplexer separates a composite signal into its component signals

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs the DAMA multiplexer and the Fleet Satellite Broadcast demultiplexer equipment models?
options: TD-1271 is the multiplexer; TD-1603 is the demultiplexer
TD-1603 is the multiplexer; TD-1271 is the demultiplexer
SA-212(V) is the multiplexer; SA-2112A(V) is the demultiplexer
USQ-144H is the multiplexer; USQ-144K(v)2 is the demultiplexer
questions.correct_answer: TD-1271 is the multiplexer; TD-1603 is the demultiplexer

questions.question: In RF patching, what physical security classifications do RED and BLACK patch panels indicate?
options: RED indicates encrypted information; BLACK indicates decrypted/unencrypted information
RED indicates decrypted/unencrypted (plain) information; BLACK indicates encrypted information
RED indicates high-power transmit lines; BLACK indicates low-power receive lines
RED indicates digital fiber connections; BLACK indicates analog copper connections
questions.correct_answer: RED indicates decrypted/unencrypted (plain) information; BLACK indicates encrypted information

questions.question: What is the operational difference between patching and switching?
options: Patching is automatic/electrical; Switching is manual/physical
Patching provides the physical/manual connections through patch panels; Switching provides electrical/automatic routing using matrices
Patching is used only on the red side; Switching is used only on the black side
Patching is for satellite antennas; Switching is for short-range whips
questions.correct_answer: Patching provides the physical/manual connections through patch panels; Switching provides electrical/automatic routing using matrices

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly maps Link 11 and Link 16 to their legacy TADIL designations?
options: Link 11 is TADIL-J; Link 16 is TADIL-A
Link 11 is TADIL-A; Link 16 is TADIL-J
Link 11 is TADIL-C; Link 16 is TADIL-B
Link 11 is Multicast; Link 16 is Unicast
questions.correct_answer: Link 11 is TADIL-A; Link 16 is TADIL-J

questions.question: What does the specialized Link system Hawklink connect?
options: Two Aegis-equipped cruisers (CG) via SHF
Ships and SH-60-family helicopters via a two-way data and voice line-of-sight path
A afloat command ship directly to the President of the United States (POTUS)
A shipboard LAN to the regional shore STEP sites
questions.correct_answer: Ships and SH-60-family helicopters via a two-way data and voice line-of-sight path

questions.question: What is the difference between Multicast TADIL J (MTJ) and Unicast TADIL J (UTJ) in tactical J-series message distribution?
options: MTJ is a physical fiber cable; UTJ is an over-the-air RF path
MTJ is one-to-many/group distribution; UTJ is one-to-one/direct distribution
MTJ is used only by submarines; UTJ is used only by helicopters
MTJ operates on HF frequencies; UTJ operates on ELF frequencies
questions.correct_answer: MTJ is one-to-many/group distribution; UTJ is one-to-one/direct distribution

questions.question: What is the core three-step Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) process?
options: DETECT -> TRACK -> DESTROY/INTERCEPT
LAUNCH -> DEFEND -> REPORT
SEARCH -> IDENTIFY -> ESCAPE
CONNECT -> ENCRYPT -> TRANSMIT
questions.correct_answer: DETECT -> TRACK -> DESTROY/INTERCEPT

questions.question: What are the different BMD roles of Standard Missile-3 (SM-3) and Standard Missile-2 (SM-2) in Aegis BMD operations?
options: SM-3 is designed for exo-atmospheric midcourse interception; SM-2 is associated with terminal/endgame phase defense
SM-3 is used exclusively against surface ships; SM-2 is used for midcourse ballistic interception
SM-3 is a land-based interceptor; SM-2 is a submarine-launched missile
SM-3 is unguided; SM-2 is guided by the SBX radar
questions.correct_answer: SM-3 is designed for exo-atmospheric midcourse interception; SM-2 is associated with terminal/endgame phase defense

questions.question: Which primary ship classes and hull designators are identified as participating in BMD-related missions?
options: Nimitz-class aircraft carriers (CVN) and Wasp-class amphibious assault ships (LHD)
Ticonderoga-class guided-missile cruisers (CG) and Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers (DDG)
Los Angeles-class fast-attack submarines (SSN) and Ohio-class ballistic missile submarines (SSBN)
Avenger-class mine countermeasures ships (MCM) and Lewis and Clark-class dry cargo ships (T-AKE)
questions.correct_answer: Ticonderoga-class guided-missile cruisers (CG) and Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers (DDG)

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Common Data Link Management System (CDLMS)?
options: It automatically rotates the ship to avoid antenna block zones during flight ops
It manages tactical data links, provides operational control, and reduces the workload on the Tactical Information Coordinator (TIC)
It converts incoming analog voice signals directly to Direct Current (DC)
It acts as a primary sensor for SPY-1 radar target tracking
questions.correct_answer: It manages tactical data links, provides operational control, and reduces the workload on the Tactical Information Coordinator (TIC)

questions.question: Which system component is explicitly identified in the study guide as the 'heart' of the TADIL/tactical configuration?
options: ESPG
HMI
MDU
C2P
questions.correct_answer: ESPG

questions.question: What is the major equipment and routing change introduced in the CDLMS V8 configuration?
options: The physical fiber-optic cables are replaced with high-speed copper links
The remote CDLMS session is sent to the CND display, and the MDU is replaced with the NIMACS console
The HMI SBC is upgraded to a liquid-cooled tactical mainframe
The entire upper chassis is eliminated, and C2P tasks are handled by the ship's gyro
questions.correct_answer: The remote CDLMS session is sent to the CND display, and the MDU is replaced with the NIMACS console

questions.question: What does the antenna principle of 'reciprocity' describe?
options: The physical tilting of whips to allow helicopter flight clearances
An antenna's ability to exhibit equivalent electrical behavior when used to transmit or receive
The automated switching between primary and secondary antennas to avoid block zones
The concentration of RF energy in one main direction rather than all directions
questions.correct_answer: An antenna's ability to exhibit equivalent electrical behavior when used to transmit or receive

questions.question: What physical trade-off occurs as an antenna's directivity increases from a wide beam to a narrow beam?
options: It increases the coverage area but requires more power
It concentrates RF energy in a precise direction, trading coverage area for concentration and accuracy
It shifts the polarization from vertical to horizontal automatically
It increases signal attenuation inside the troposphere
questions.correct_answer: It concentrates RF energy in a precise direction, trading coverage area for concentration and accuracy

questions.question: What is a 'block zone' in shipboard antenna operations, and how do operators resolve it?
options: A software lock on unclassified routers; resolved by logging into the NOC
An area where the ship's physical structure obstructs an antenna's RF path; resolved by changing ship heading or selecting another antenna
A magnetic disturbance near the earth's poles; resolved by tuning the HF coupler
A high-noise area exceeding 85 dB; resolved by wearing double ear protection
questions.correct_answer: An area where the ship's physical structure obstructs an antenna's RF path; resolved by changing ship heading or selecting another antenna

questions.question: What is the purpose and signal flow of the AS-2815/SSR-1 satellite antenna?
options: It is an omnidirectional, receive-only antenna used to pick up satellite broadcast traffic
It is a directional, transmit-only antenna used to report missile tracks to POTUS
It is a gyroscope-driven tracking antenna used to connect the shipboard LAN to the pier
It is a circular mast-clamp antenna used for JTIDS line-of-sight voice circuits
questions.correct_answer: It is an omnidirectional, receive-only antenna used to pick up satellite broadcast traffic

questions.question: Which of the following describes the physical structure and coverage of the AS-4163 'Stovepipe' antenna?
options: A circular mast-clamp antenna used exclusively for JTIDS
A dual-channel UHF antenna featuring two independent broadband elements inside a fiberglass radome, providing omnidirectional coverage
A 35-foot flexible vertical whip mounted on an antenna tilt group
A flat-plated directional antenna consisting of four panels
questions.correct_answer: A dual-channel UHF antenna featuring two independent broadband elements inside a fiberglass radome, providing omnidirectional coverage

questions.question: What is the nickname and mounting style of the AS-4172A antenna associated with JTIDS?
options: Nickname 'Spider'; mounted as a vertical whip on the weather deck
Nickname 'Stovepipe'; mounted high on the superstructure in a radome
Nickname 'Dog Bowl'; circular mast-clamp type
Nickname 'Red Cabinet'; mounted inside the Combat Information Center (CIC)
questions.correct_answer: Nickname 'Dog Bowl'; circular mast-clamp type

questions.question: What is the primary operational benefit of utilizing a dual-antenna configuration in the OE-82 SATCOM antenna group?
options: It doubles the data rate of the Fleet Satellite Broadcast
It allows the ship to transmit unclassified and top secret data simultaneously
It helps maintain continuous satellite visibility and reduces block-zone problems as the ship moves
It eliminates the need for any internal coupling or signal processing
questions.correct_answer: It helps maintain continuous satellite visibility and reduces block-zone problems as the ship moves

questions.question: Which of the following describes the AN/WSC-5(V) satellite antenna?
options: A small, circular mast-clamp antenna used ship-to-helicopter
A major shore-station SATCOM antenna pedestal group that is manually oriented and locked after satellite acquisition
A 35-foot fiberglass vertical whip used for long-range HF communications
A legacy ADNS hardware variant being retired from the fleet
questions.correct_answer: A major shore-station SATCOM antenna pedestal group that is manually oriented and locked after satellite acquisition

questions.question: Why are certain shipboard whip antennas attached to tilt groups so they can be tilted from a vertical to a horizontal position?
options: To shift polarization from vertical to horizontal for better surface wave propagation
To support flight operations and meet clearance requirements
To increase directivity toward satellite orbits during extreme weather
To prevent electrical shocks when cleaning components with steel wool
questions.correct_answer: To support flight operations and meet clearance requirements
